In 2009, the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Alliance for Health Policy and Systems Research published a report titled Systems Thinking for Health Systems Strengthening, which emphasized the importance of a systems-based approach to improving health systems. 2. A 2014 study by Benvenuti et al. investigated the effectiveness of community-based exercise programs for individuals with upper limb paresis, incorporating tele-rehabilitation. The findings were published in Neurorehabilitation and Neural Repair. 3. A randomized controlled trial conducted in 2006 by Beland et al. evaluated an integrated care system for older adults with disabilities in Canada. The results, published in The Journals of Gerontology: Series A, demonstrated the benefits of such a system. 4. Fisher and Savin-Baden (2001) assessed the advantages of early intervention programs for young individuals experiencing psychosis and their families. Their evaluation, based on consumer and provider perspectives, was published in the British Journal of Occupational Therapy. 5. Tedesco et al. (2011) explored professional nurses' perceptions of occupational therapy interventions in mental health settings at a university hospital. Their findings were published in Acta Paulista de Enfermagem. 6. Kamm et al. (2014) examined interdisciplinary outpatient rehabilitation programs for patients recovering from transient ischemic attacks or strokes with minimal residual deficits. The study, published in Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, highlighted the benefits of such programs. 7. The BRIGHTEN program, evaluated by Emery et al. in 2012, focused on bridging resources for interdisciplinary geriatric health teams through electronic networking. The results were published in The Gerontologist. 8. Jessep et al. (2009) compared the long-term clinical benefits and costs of an integrated rehabilitation program versus outpatient physiotherapy for chronic knee pain. Their findings were published in Physiotherapy. 9. Forster et al. (2008) conducted a Cochrane review comparing medical day hospital care for the elderly with alternative care models. The review highlighted the effectiveness of day hospital care. 10. Karjalainen et al. (2003) conducted two Cochrane reviews on multidisciplinary biopsychosocial rehabilitation for subacute low back pain and neck/shoulder pain among working-age adults. These reviews emphasized the benefits of such approaches. 11. Ng et al. (2009) reviewed multidisciplinary care for adults with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) or motor neuron disease. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 12. Turner-Stokes et al. (2015) evaluated multidisciplinary rehabilitation for adults with acquired brain injuries. Their Cochrane review highlighted the importance of such interventions for working-age individuals. 13. Lincoln et al. (2004) assessed the effectiveness of a multiprofessional community stroke team through a randomized controlled trial. The results were published in Clinical Rehabilitation. 14. Cullen et al. (1997) compared client satisfaction with case management for individuals with mental illness. Their findings were published in Health & Social Care in the Community. 15. Berry (2007) explored the needs of service users and staff perceptions regarding psychology services in psychiatric rehabilitation. The study was published in Clinical Psychology & Psychotherapy. 16. Gage et al. (2011) designed a randomized controlled trial protocol to compare specialist rehabilitation and care assistant support for individuals with Parkinson’s disease living in the community. The study was published in Trials. 17. The WHO (2010) released global policy recommendations to improve health worker retention in remote and rural areas, emphasizing strategies to increase access to healthcare. 18. Anderson et al. (2000) conducted a cost-minimization analysis comparing home-based and hospital-based stroke rehabilitation. The findings were published in Stroke. 19. Fjaertoft et al. (2003) evaluated the long-term outcomes of stroke unit care combined with early supported discharge. The study, published in Stroke, demonstrated the benefits of this approach. 20. Kalra et al. (2005) conducted a randomized controlled trial comparing alternative strategies in stroke care. The findings were published in Health Technology Assessment. 21. Donnelly et al. (2004) evaluated an early discharge rehabilitation service through the Belfast Community Stroke Trial. The results were published in Stroke. 22. Taylor et al. (2010) reviewed home-based versus center-based cardiac rehabilitation programs. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 23. Jolliffe et al. (2000) conducted a Cochrane review on exercise-based rehabilitation for coronary heart disease, highlighting its effectiveness. 24. Taylor et al. (2004) performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of exercise-based rehabilitation for coronary heart disease patients. The study was published in The American Journal of Medicine. 25. Taylor et al. (2014) reviewed exercise-based rehabilitation for heart failure patients. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 26. Wells et al. (2013) conducted a community-partnered cluster-randomized trial to address depression disparities through community engagement and planning. The study was published in Journal of General Internal Medicine. 27. Burns et al. (2001) systematically reviewed home treatment for mental health problems. The findings were published in Health Technology Assessment. 28. Caplan et al. (2006) evaluated the impact of home treatment on delirium through the REACH-OUT trial. The study was published in Age and Ageing. 29. Beswick et al. (2008) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of complex interventions aimed at improving physical function and maintaining independence in elderly individuals. The findings were published in The Lancet. 30. Dixon et al. (2015) assessed patient preferences for community-based care models using a discrete choice experiment. The study was published in Health Expectations. 31. Gilbertson and Langhorne (2000) evaluated home-based occupational therapy for stroke patients, focusing on satisfaction with occupational performance and service provision. The study was published in British Journal of Occupational Therapy. 32. Henderson et al. (1999) compared patient satisfaction with community-based versus hospital psychiatric services. The findings were published in Acta Psychiatrica Scandinavica. 33. Jester and Hicks (2003) analyzed the cost-effectiveness of hospital-at-home versus inpatient interventions. The study was published in Journal of Clinical Nursing. 34. Families of adults with severe mental illness expressed their satisfaction with inpatient and outpatient treatment in a study published in Psychosocial Rehabilitation Journal in 1992. 35. Utens et al. (2013) evaluated patient preferences and satisfaction with hospital-at-home versus usual hospital care for COPD exacerbations. The study was published in International Journal of Nursing Studies. 36. Chatterjee et al. (2009) assessed outcomes of individuals with psychotic disorders in a community-based rehabilitation program in rural India. The findings were published in The British Journal of Psychiatry. 37. Court et al. (2011) evaluated the effectiveness of the Welsh low vision service, a community-based program. The study was published in British Journal of Ophthalmology. 38. Copolillo and Ivanoff (2011) reviewed assistive technology and home modifications for individuals with neurovisual deficits. The findings were published in Neurorehabilitation. 39. Wolfe et al. (2012) summarized rehabilitation practices and outcomes following spinal cord injury in a report by the SCIRe Project. 40. Mossialos and Dixon (2002) provided an introduction to healthcare funding in Europe, discussing various options in their book published by Open University Press. 41. The WHO (2016) outlined the concept of universal health coverage in a report titled Health Financing for Universal Coverage. 42. Harvey et al. (1998) identified clinical predictors of resource utilization in stroke rehabilitation. The study was published in Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation. 43. Brusco et al. (2014) conducted an economic evaluation of adult rehabilitation across various settings. The findings were published in Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation. 44. Green et al. (2000) examined resource allocation and budgeting mechanisms in decentralized health systems, focusing on experiences in Baluchistan, Pakistan. The study was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 45. Puhan et al. (2011) reviewed pulmonary rehabilitation following COPD exacerbations. The findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 46. Ayanian et al. The study was published in JAMA. 47. Iezzoni et al. The findings were published in Disability and Health Journal. 48. Ross et al. The study was published in JAMA. 49. Kogan et al. (2010) examined underinsurance among children in the United States. The findings were published in The New England Journal of Medicine. 50. Skinner and Mayer (2007) reviewed the effects of insurance status on children’s access to specialty care. The study was published in BMC Health Services Research. 51. Buchanan et al. (2010) explored informal caregivers’ perceptions of health and support services for individuals with multiple sclerosis. The findings were published in Disability and Rehabilitation. 52. Jeffrey and Newacheck (2006) synthesized evidence on the role of insurance for children with special healthcare needs. The study was published in Pediatrics. 53. The WHO (2016) emphasized global cooperation on assistive technology in a report. 54. Borg and Khasnabis (2008) provided guidelines on manual wheelchair provision in resource-limited settings in a WHO publication. 55. The WHO (2008) addressed challenges and choices in scaling up health services in a report. 56. The WHO (2001) introduced the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health. 57. Waddington and Egger (2008) discussed integrated health services in a WHO technical brief. 58. The WHO outlined its guideline development process, emphasizing the roles of the Secretariat, Guideline Development Group, and External Review Group in producing evidence-based recommendations.
